extracted.subtask_description: A compilation of Associated Press news dispatches covering international relations, military operations and personnel, legislative summaries (economic mobilization bill), casualty lists, and government decisions. Intended as a daily news roundup for public consumption and downstream editorial use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 101(A) — Presidential authority on priorities and allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to require that contracts he deems necessary or appropriate to promote the national defense shall be accepted and performed by any person found to be capable of performance, and be given preference over all other contracts; authorizes allocation of materials and facilities on such terms as he may deem appropriate to promote the national defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of this authority to ration consumer goods at the retail level is expressly prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 101(B) — Criminal penalties for violations of Title I
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides criminal penalties for willful violations of the provisions of Title I or of any rule or regulation issued thereunder.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 201 — Authority to requisition materials and facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to requisition materials and facilities urgently needed for the national defense, with payment of just compensation as determined by the President.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the person is not willing to accept compensation as full payment, he shall be paid 50 per cent of the amount and shall be entitled to sue for the remainder within three years in the Court of Claims or any district court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 301(A) — Loan guarantees for defense purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to provide for the guaranty of loans made by public or private financial institutions to contractors or other persons for defense purposes; may authorize Defense Departments and other government agencies to make such guarantees without regard to laws relating to making, performance, amendment or modification of contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates Federal Reserve Banks to act as fiscal agents to carry out such guarantees and provides for utilization of funds of the guaranteeing agency to meet all expenses and losses incurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 301(C) — Federal Reserve Board authority over loan-guarantee terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the Federal Reserve Board to prescribe rates of interest and other charges and to issue regulations governing uniform procedures for loan guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 302 — Loans for expansion, development, or production
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives the President authority to provide loans to private business enterprises for expansion of capacity, development of technological processes, or production of essential materials; loans may be made on such terms and conditions as the President deems necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two exceptions: (1) other financial assistance must be unavailable on reasonable terms; (2) portion of loan principal used for plant or equipment may not exceed 75 percent of the cost of such plant or equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 303(A) — Purchase authority for raw materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to make purchases or commitments to purchase metals, minerals and other raw materials as are necessary to meet military and essential civilian needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removes procurement restrictions of other laws and permits advance payments and other terms; use of premium payments is confined to cases where supply cannot be obtained at lower prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 303(C) — Incidental powers for purchases
rubrics_metrics.description: States that the power to purchase includes the power to transport, store, process and refine any materials procured under this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 304 — Administration and creation/use of corporations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to utilize the Reconstruction Finance Corporation and other agencies or to create and use new corporations for purposes of sections 302 and 303.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Life of such corporations is limited to June 30, 1952 (except for liquidation); authorization to borrow from the Treasury may not exceed $2,000,000,000; arrangements for issuance of corporate obligations to the Secretary of the Treasury are prescribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 401(A) — Controls over consumer and real estate credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides authority similar to Regulation W during the past war and adds controls over real property credit; authorizes the President to classify transactions and prescribe maximum loans or credit values, minimum down payments, rules regarding outstanding credit and other related matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations may include administrative provisions taking into account changing conditions as to level and trend of consumer and real estate credit and the effect on purchasing power, demand for real property and the need for maintenance of sound credit conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 401(B) — Compliance, recordkeeping and examinations for credit businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides that no person engaged in the business of extending or maintaining consumer or real estate credit shall extend or maintain any credit or do any act in contravention of any regulation prescribed by the President; requires keeping records and making reports as may be required; records subject to periodic or other examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 401(C) — Penalties for violations in consumer/real estate credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides penalties for violations of this act or of regulations issued thereunder pertaining to consumer and real estate credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 401(D) — Registration and licensing authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides that transactions and persons subject to this section may be required to be registered or licensed; such registration or license may be suspended for violation after notice and opportunity for hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes utilization of the Federal Reserve Board, Federal Reserve Banks, and any other appropriate federal or state agencies in administering this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 401(E) — Definitions for Title IV
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines terms applicable to Title IV (consumer and real estate credit provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 401 (Housing loans provision) — Reduction of terms for government-participating housing loans
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to reduce maximum principal amounts, maximum maturities and ratios of loan to value or cost of any type of housing loan in which any government agency participates whenever he finds, after considering the effect on the building industry, national economy, and defense production, such action is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes proviso requiring retention of a relative preference for veterans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 403 — Amendment to Federal Home Loan Bank Act
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides against the making or purchase of any loan by a member of a Federal Home Loan Bank when its cash and obligations of the United States are not equal to such amount as prescribed by the Home Loan Bank Board within prescribed limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 411 Paragraph 5(A) — Commodity speculation margin authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Adds a Paragraph to the Commodity Exchange Act permitting the President, upon determination that speculative trading causes or threatens sudden or unreasonable price fluctuations in any commodity, to prescribe regulations as to margin for purchase or sale of such commodity for future delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 411 Paragraph 5(B) — Margin deposit requirement and floor broker exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides that buying, selling or accepting orders for purchase or sale of such commodity for future delivery is unlawful unless margin funds or securities are deposited and maintained in compliance with rules and regulations promulgated under this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A floor broker acting solely in that capacity shall not be deemed a violator of this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 411 Paragraph 5(D) — Recordkeeping and inspection for commodity orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides that persons soliciting or accepting orders for purchase or sale of a commodity for future delivery must keep written records of such transactions for three years from date of each transaction, and make them open at all times to inspection by any designated government representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 411 Paragraph 5(E) — Definition of 'commodity'
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides that the term 'commodity' includes agricultural commodity, product or by-product thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 411 Paragraph 5(F) — Enforcement tie-in to securities law
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides that the provisions of Section 21 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, are made applicable for administering and enforcing this Paragraph 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 412 — Commodity Credit Corporation authority to stabilize markets
rubrics_metrics.description: Amends the Agricultural Act of 1949 to authorize the Commodity Credit Corporation, when the President so directs, to sell commodities at the current support price (if not below market price) for the purpose of stabilizing the market and preventing undue speculation and price fluctuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 501 — Small business participation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Expresses the policy of encouraging participation of small firms in programs authorized by the act; provides for full information concerning government agency activities and for appropriate representation of small business on industry advisory committees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides for exemptions for small firms where feasible and procedures to expedite their applications, requests and appeals related to such participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 502 — Definitions provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines key terms used in the act (e.g., 'person' and 'materials').

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 503 — Delegations of authority and personnel employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Allows any power conferred upon the President by the act to be delegated and redelegated to any officer or agency; authorizes personnel to carry out the purposes of the act without regard to certain provisions of the Federal Employees Pay Act of 1946.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 504 — Authority to issue rules and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to issue rules and regulations necessary to implement the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 505(A) — Information, records and subpoena power
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to require keeping of records, submission of reports, inspection of books, premises or property, and attendance of witnesses by subpoena or otherwise as may be necessary or appropriate to enforcement or administration of the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 505(B) — Testimony and production immunity (limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides that any individual may be required to testify or produce evidence despite a claim of privilege against self-incrimination but may not be prosecuted or penalized, except for perjury, on account of any transaction covered by such testimony or evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This immunity does not insure such a violator further priorities assistance or allocation of materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 505(C) — Limits on production of books and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits the production of a person's books or records to the place where he usually keeps them if he will furnish the President with a true copy of such books or records or stipulates as to the information contained therein; fees and mileage for witnesses same as in U.S. courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 505(D) — Confidentiality and criminal penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides for non-disclosure of information deemed confidential by the President or requested as confidential by the person supplying it, with criminal penalties provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 506 — Enforcement jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants the district courts of the United States and courts of territories jurisdiction of violations of the act or regulations, and of all civil actions or injunctions arising out of the act or rules thereunder; includes provisions for jurisdiction, process, and subpoena of witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 507 — Exculpatory clause for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides an exemption from damage suits resulting from compliance with rules, regulations or orders issued pursuant to the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 508 — Anti-trust exemption for Presidential requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides that no act or omission to act requested by the President under the act shall be construed to be within the prohibition of the anti-trust laws or the Federal Trade Commission Act; copies of such requests shall be furnished to the Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority granted in this section shall be delegated only to a single official required to consult with the Attorney General concerning each request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 509 — Administrative Procedure Act (APA) exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Declares that functions of the act are excluded from operation of the Administrative Procedure Act except as to requirements of Section 3 thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 510 — Exemption from Classification Act limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes the President to place positions and employ persons in civil service grades 16, 17, and 18 without regard to numbers authorized by Section 505 of the Classification Act of 1949.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 511 — Appropriations and fund transfers
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizes appropriations necessary to carry out the provisions and purposes of the act and authorizes transfer of funds to any agency designated to assist in carrying out functions under the act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sec. 512 — Termination of authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: States that the act and all authority conferred thereunder shall terminate June 30, 1952.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-bomb plant site selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Site selection for a hydrogen-bomb production plant should include as much as 200,900 acres and must consider an important element: selection of a location that would 'minimize its vulnerability to enemy attack.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement also notes plan not to build a new government-owned community as was done at Oak Ridge and Los Alamos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for calling reservists (skills-based prioritization)
rubrics_metrics.description: In selective call-up emphasis is on individuals with immediately usable skills such as electronics experts, airborne operations, tank and armament maintenance, construction (bridges, roads, ports, airfields), navigators, bombardiers, communications, radio and radar specialists, medical and dental officers, weather specialists and armament officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services indicated some organized reserve units as well as individual reservists will be called; certain critical specialists may be required in other grades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navy deferment policy for reserve call-up
rubrics_metrics.description: No deferments will be granted except in cases involving key industrial jobs vital to defense or where community welfare would be seriously affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naval quotas to be filled as far as possible from the organized reserve who are to be qualified for active duty and from the fleet reserve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum active service term for called reservists
rubrics_metrics.description: All three services said they intend to provide a minimum of one year's service for reservists ordered to extended active duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reservists may continue to volunteer for active duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on reserve officers' grades upon recall
rubrics_metrics.description: Reserve officers returned to active duty, either by volunteering or being called up, will keep their latest reserve grades; reserve officers holding the rank of major or higher but already on active duty in a lower rank will be considered for promotion before there is any general recall of reserve officers of comparable rank.
